title: 2026 is the year AI is pushed to production
summary: “Two years ago, AI was a demo. Last year, it was a pilot. This year, the leaders who are pulling ahead have moved it into production.” At this year’s VST ECS’ CXO Summit,…

blocks.text: “Two years ago, AI was a demo. Last year, it was a pilot. This year, the leaders who are pulling ahead have moved it into production.”

At this year’s VST ECS’ CXO Summit, President and CEO Jimmy Go laid down the new realities of the AI disruption for Philippine industries. Go tempered optimism with industry challenges. Two years ago, Philippine companies were looking at AI from the lens of curiosity. At last year’s summit, these same companies were piloting AI programs within their own departments or entire organizations. This year, the trend is all about making AI work in order to bring quantifiable gains either in revenue or productivity.

blocks.caption: Jimmy Go President and CEO of VST ECS

blocks.text: AI landscape in the local context

Go cited how the Philippines is making waves in the right direction for AI with data sovereignty, the Pax Silica initiative, and local headways from large hyperscalers like AWS’ USD $5 Billion investment. He also spoke of the Philippine advantage, which is a young population of social media savvy individuals who are the most capable and unafraid of using AI for upskilling.

This also comes at a time where the AI boom has caused pricing to increase drastically, with HBM supply locked until 2027. This has caused a ripple effect with consumer-level smartphones, laptops, and other related technology to increase in pricing by more than 60%.

There have been headwinds made across industries in the Philippines with AI adoption. In the healthcare industry, it’s using predictive AI to discover life-saving molecules within days versus decades. With logistics, it’s about deploying autonomous systems to upgrade or even replace legacy systems. In finance, it’s about using AI to detect fraud by processing millions of micro-transactions.
According to data from VST ECS, there has been a huge shift in enterprise spend and pricing.

For Servers & Storage, allocation shifted heavily toward hyperscalers. Enterprise IT deployments slipped into 2027. Server high-speed DDR5 prices rose nearly 100% quarter on quarter, inflating budgets and delaying smaller enterprise rollouts.

PCs & Notebooks reduced shipments, redesigned configurations, and in some cases downgraded specs. Consumer notebook prices rose 30–50%, with higher costs for midrange models. Smartphones also had rising costs, forcing brands to raise prices or cut shipment targets. IDC projected a 13% drop in global smartphone sales in 2026.

Go’s message to IT decision makers is that despite these fluctuations in the market, in order to remain competitive, you cannot wait for a perfect product to be revealed. As large language models are being improved every month, and memory prices are fluctuating every quarter, it may be tempting to wait. He says that “Waiting for a technology to become perfectly stable before adopting it is a death sentence. By then, others will have already scaled it and captured the advantage. In this era, agility is the real form of risk management.”
